required_interface: kellogg v2 attestation envelope: `zeckendorf` field is an int (11-bit token from kellogg/scales.py::zeckendorf_11d); `cassini` is the list field
reason: tests/test_kellogg_production_evidence_boundary.py lines ~82-85 corrupts the envelope with `corrupt_zeckendorf["zeckendorf"] = list(corrupt_zeckendorf["zeckendorf"]) + [1]` — TypeError: 'int' object is not iterable against the shipped schema. Suggested one-line fix: `corrupt_zeckendorf["zeckendorf"] = int(corrupt_zeckendorf["zeckendorf"]) + 1` (or `^= 1`); the digest-binding tamper check still fires. Test asserted list semantics the implementation never had — implementation is correct, test is stale.

tests/test_sequential_contracts.py::test_claims_registry_loads_and_evaluates_clean fails: the claims registry flags PROHIBITED `10 EH/s` in docs/FAULT_TOLERANT_QUANTUM_ASIC.md line 5. required_interface: kellogg-tensor must build/install as a wheel on setuptools >= 77
reason: packaging/kellogg-tensor/pyproject.toml declares both `license = "MIT"` (PEP 639 SPDX expression) and the deprecated classifier `License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License`. setuptools >= 77 rejects the combination with InvalidConfigError ('License classifiers have been superseded by license expressions'), so `pip install` of the staged kellogg-tensor dist fails — blocking the documented TURING install chain (`pip install -e ./turing_universal_quantum_computer` requires kellogg-tensor>=1.0). Fix: drop the license classifier, keep `license = "MIT"`. Agent D verified the fix works on a locally staged copy.

required_interface: exact-vqc TypeScript tests need node >= 22.6 for `node --experimental-strip-types`; proofs/ needs a Lean/lake toolchain
reason: turing_universal_quantum_computer/exact-vqc/README.md records `node --experimental-strip-types --test src/lib/vqc/*.test.ts` (24 passing) and `tsc --noEmit` as its gate; the session VM ships node v20.19.0, which does not support --experimental-strip-types, so the suite cannot execute there. proofs/ (Lean kernels: zeta_8 periodicity, even-overlap commutation) has no Lean toolchain on the VM. Both are tooling/environment gaps, not code defects — recorded for CI image/toolchain provisioning.
